identity.title: List of digital home video releases of Pokémon animation

source.sourceCategory: Category:Lists of animation home video releases

leadText:
The following is a list of all of the home video releases of the Pokémon animation available for purchase on digital platforms such as the iTunes Store, Google Play, and Prime Video (this page does not list releases available for streaming on platforms such as Netflix or Hulu). Most releases are available in the United States, , , and .

It contains the Pokémon animated series, Pokémon Origins as well as the s. All releases have English closed captions available.
plainText:
The following is a list of all of the home video releases of the Pokémon animation available for purchase on digital platforms such as the iTunes Store, Google Play, and Prime Video (this page does not list releases available for streaming on platforms such as Netflix or Hulu). Most releases are available in the United States, , , and .

It contains the Pokémon animated series, Pokémon Origins as well as the s. All releases have English closed captions available.

==Pokémon the Series: The Beginning==
Unlike previous releases of the first season, the videos used for this release have been remastered and are available in HD. They are also used on the service and on Blu-ray releases. The Kanto Pokérap is included, but the Who's That Pokémon? segments are not.

The first season is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
Amazon Video: English (United States, United Kingdom; except EP051)
Google TV/YouTube: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)

The second season is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
English (United States)

The second season can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States, United Kingdom)

 

===Pokémon Collections===
These are Pokémon Collections volumes, which select particular episodes to include from various points in the series, rather than a sequence of episodes. The Kanto Pokérap and Who's That Pokémon? segments are included.

It is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
Amazon Video: English (United States, United Kingdom)
Google Play: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)

 

==Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver==
These releases are only available on Amazon Video.

The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany; except S05, Vol. 2)

The series can be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States)
French (France)
German (Germany; only S05, Vol. 2)
Italian (Italy)
Brazilian Portuguese (Brazil)
Latin American Spanish (Latin America)
European Spanish (Spain)

The series can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United Kingdom)

In the United Kingdom, the series has separate individual volume listings which can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription, distinct from the standard individual volumes for purchase.

 

===Pokémon Collections===
These are Pokémon Collections volumes, which select particular episodes to include from various points in the series, rather than a sequence of episodes.

It is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
Amazon Video: English (United States, United Kingdom)
Google Play: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)

 

==Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire==
This release does not include the Who's That Pokémon? and Pokémon Trainer's Choice segments, as well as the season-based eyecatches from the final commercial breaks.

Previously, the Amazon volumes used similar artwork to the iTunes releases.

This series can currently no longer be purchased on the iTunes Store, despite previously having been available.

The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play: English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)

The series can be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States)
Danish (Denmark)
Dutch (Netherlands)
French (France)
German (Germany)
Italian (Italy)
Brazilian Portuguese (Brazil)
Latin American Spanish (Latin America)
European Spanish (Spain)
Swedish (Sweden)

In Germany, the series has separate individual volume listings which can be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription, distinct from the standard individual volumes for purchase.

 

==Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl==
These releases are only available on Amazon Video. Previously, the Amazon volumes used different artwork with a -pattern background.

The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
English (United States, United Kingdom)

The series can be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription in the following languages and territories:
Czech (Czech Republic)
Danish (Denmark)
Dutch (Netherlands)
Finnish (Finland)
French (France)
German (Germany)
Italian (Italy)
Polish (Poland)
Latin American Spanish (Latin America)
European Spanish (Spain)
Swedish (Sweden)

Sinnoh League Victors had a separate full season listing which could be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription, distinct from the standard individual volumes for purchase, although this is currently no longer available.

 

==Pokémon the Series: Black & White==
These releases are only available on Amazon Video.

The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
English (United States, United Kingdom)

The series can be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)

The series can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States; United Kingdom)

The series had separate full season listings which could be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription, distinct from the standard individual volumes for purchase, although this is currently no longer available.

In the United Kingdom, the series has separate individual volume listings which can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription, distinct from the standard individual volumes for purchase.

 

==Pokémon the Series: XY==
Previously, the Amazon volumes used different artwork similar to the iTunes releases but with a different font for the season and volume number. In the United Kingdom, the Amazon volumes use the same artwork as the old Amazon volumes in the United States for XY and the second half of XY Kalos Quest, the new Amazon volumes for XYZ, or different artwork that more closely resembles the iTunes releases for the first half of XY Kalos Quest.

The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France; S19 only)
German (Germany; S19 only)
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France; S19 only)
German (Germany; S19 only)

The series can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United Kingdom)

In the United Kingdom, the series has separate individual volume listings which can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription, distinct from the standard individual volumes for purchase.

 

==Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon==
Previously, the iTunes artwork for the second volume of Sun & Moon featured instead of and the Amazon artwork for the third volume of Ultra Legends used a generic image rather than a volume specific image.

The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)

The series can be streamed with a Pokémon on Amazon subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States)

In the United Kingdom, the first volume for season 20 has two separate individual volume listings for purchase.

 

==Pokémon Journeys: The Series==
The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)

 

==Pokémon Horizons: The Series==
The series is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)

 

==Movies==
On Amazon Video, a rotating selection of movies can be streamed with the Pokémon channel subscription for Amazon Prime members.

Celebi: The Voice of the Forest was previously released on January 19, 2016, but was removed from sale sometime in 2017. It was later released again along with Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias on December 13, 2023, after the rights to both films were obtained by from their prior distributor Miramax. Jirachi: Wish Maker and Destiny Deoxys were previously released by Miramax in February 2022, but were removed from sale sometime in July 2024; they were released again by TPCi on August 27, 2024.

The animated movies are available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France, Belgium)
German (Germany, Austria, Luxembourg)
Italian (Italy)
European Spanish (Spain)
Latin American Spanish (Argentina, Belize, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Venezuela)
Brazilian Portuguese (Brazil)
Dutch (Netherlands)
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France, Belgium)
German (Germany, Austria, Luxembourg)
Italian (Italy)
European Spanish (Spain)
Latin American Spanish (Mexico)
Brazilian Portuguese (Brazil)

 

===Live-action===
 

==Specials==
On Amazon Video, Pokémon Origins can currently be streamed with the Pokémon channel subscription for Amazon Prime members.

Pokémon Origins is available for purchase in the following languages and territories:
iTunes:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)
Amazon Video:
English (United States, United Kingdom)
German (Germany)
Google Play:
English (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)
French (France)
German (Germany)

Although currently no longer available, Pokémon Generations was previously able to be streamed for free with a Prime Video subscription in the following languages and territories:
English (United States)

 

==Trivia==
Similar series, season, and volume divisions to the ones first used in the digital home video releases were formerly used on Pokémon TV.

==External links==
Pokémon on Prime Video (US)
Pokémon on Amazon Prime Video (UK)
